title: docs: first-screen LCP is read over HTTPS with HTTP/2, and self-hosting recommends serving HTTP/2
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-sales"} -->
_Requested by **Sales** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu?thread=cmsg_01D5bWFY3rFzgJcytD5gD4Uu2qzrpapiEtaSS8VNGQmWkU)_

Part of #37444. Writes the card's amended acceptance condition (maintainer ruling 7205984444: first-screen LCP is read on a production build over HTTPS with HTTP/2, and an HTTP/1.1 reading is a control only) into the checklist item the run is recorded against, and states in the deployment docs that HTTP/2 is the recommended setup. The card stays open: list and record pages still miss 2500 ms.

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化：自己部署的用户会在部署文档里看到「对浏览器开启 HTTP/2」的建议、原因和检查方法，上线清单多一条；测试清单里首屏 2.5 秒那一项改为按 HTTPS + HTTP/2 读数。产品本身不变。
- 为什么做：你 23:53Z 同意了首屏验收按 HTTPS + HTTP/2 量。首屏大约 150 个脚本请求在 HTTP/1.1 下只能排在 6 条连接上，同一构建慢 1.4–2 秒，这是真实部署不会付的代价。
- 出错会怎样：只是文档和测试清单的文字；最坏情况是某句说法不准，改一句即可。
- 要你做什么：无。

## What changes

- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/ux-conventions.json`, item `ux-conventions.first-screen-lcp`, revision 1 → 2:
  - the title names the condition (a production build served over HTTPS with HTTP/2);
  - `requires`: the boot is a production one (`objectstack start` with `NODE_ENV=production`), and a new entry requires an HTTPS front speaking HTTP/2 (a deployment's own, or a local TLS front with a self-signed certificate), with the reason;
  - the persona says how to sign in on a production boot (it refuses the dev seed password; `os user set-password` sets one);
  - step 1 confirms the document's protocol is `h2` (with `--disable-quic` where the front also offers HTTP/3); step 5 records the protocol and allows an HTTP/1.1 reading only as a control;
  - a new acceptance clause: every scored run was served over HTTP/2, read from each report's `audits['network-requests']` script items (`protocol` is `h2`) and the navigation entry's `nextHopProtocol`;
  - a new `negative` row: an HTTP/1.1, HTTP/3 or development-boot reading neither passes nor fails a clause;
  - `source` cites ruling 7205984444; a `history` row names every changed field and records the reading at the new condition (median of 5: home 2297, list 2837, record 2685 ms; HTTP/1.1 control, median of 3: 3689 / 4788 / 4309 ms; per-run values in #37444 comment 7204645317).
- `content/docs/deployment/self-hosting.mdx`: a new subsection, *Serve HTTP/2 to browsers*, at the end of *Reverse proxy & TLS*. It says why (well over a hundred scripts before the first screen, about 120 on every page; six HTTP/1.1 connections per origin; 1.4–2 s measured on the same build), that the runtime's own HTTP/1.1 is fine behind the proxy, how Caddy, cloud load balancers and nginx turn it on, and how to check it in DevTools.
- `content/docs/deployment/production-readiness.mdx`: a go-live checklist line linking to that subsection.

No code changes. Docs and the QA checklist publish nothing from any released package, so this takes `skip-changeset`.

## Tests

- `pnpm check:platform-checklist` exit 0 (448 items; the revision bump and history row pass its revision/history check).
- `pnpm check:doc-anchors` exit 0 (the new `#serve-http2-to-browsers` link resolves).

## Acceptance notes

- The ~150 figure is the one in the protocol finding (#37444 comment 7204645317) and the ruling: the script requests Lighthouse queues before the first screen on the showcase. The runs fetch 194–246 script requests in all, some of them after first paint.
- The 1.4–2 s figure is home 3689 − 2297, list 4788 − 2837, record 4309 − 2685 ms, the same production build at main `9476092c` through the same local TLS front with and without HTTP/2.
- nginx syntax: `http2 on;` from 1.25.1; `listen 443 ssl http2;` before it.
- L2 owed (not self-reviewed); no governed path.
